questions.question: In a Neo4j graph of people, each KNOWS link between two person nodes is stored as a first-class object that can carry its own properties such as 'since'. What are these connections called?
questions.explanation: Edges (relationships in Neo4j terminology) connect nodes and, unlike a join, are stored directly with type, direction, and properties of their own.

questions.question: A Cassandra client writing financial records refuses to report success until every one of the 3 replicas has acknowledged the write. Which consistency level does it use?
questions.explanation: ALL requires acknowledgment from every replica, giving the strongest write durability but the worst availability — one unreachable replica fails the write.

questions.question: With replication factor 5, a Cassandra write must be acknowledged by a strict majority of replicas — at least 3 — before it reports success. Which consistency level enforces this?
questions.explanation: QUORUM waits for floor(N/2) + 1 = 3 of 5 replicas, so a quorum read and a quorum write always overlap on at least one up-to-date replica.

questions.question: When a MongoDB replica set's primary fails, the secondaries hold an election in which a majority of voting members picks the new primary. Which consensus protocol drives this election?
questions.explanation: MongoDB's replica-set elections are based on a Raft-like consensus protocol: a candidate must win a majority of votes in a term to become primary.

questions.question: MATCH (a:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(b:Person) RETURN b — which declarative graph query language is this statement written in?
questions.explanation: Cypher is Neo4j's pattern-matching query language; ASCII-art patterns like (a)-[:KNOWS]->(b) describe graph structures to find.

questions.question: A shopping-cart write returns success immediately, but a read served by another node moments later may still show the old cart; if writes stop, all replicas converge to the new value. Which consistency model is this?
questions.explanation: Eventual consistency guarantees convergence only in the absence of new updates, trading immediate consistency for availability and partition tolerance.

questions.question: A startup wants a fully managed AWS key-value/document store that scales horizontally, delivers single-digit-millisecond reads, and offers tunable strong-versus-eventual consistency. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value and document store, inspired by the Dynamo paper's eventual-consistency design, with optional strongly consistent reads.

questions.question: To serve the order-details page in a single read, the team copies the customer's name and address into every order document rather than joining collections. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Denormalization duplicates related data into the queried document to avoid joins, trading storage and update cost for single-lookup reads.

questions.question: Built at Facebook for inbox search, this open-source column-family store arranges nodes in a masterless ring and favors availability during partitions. Which database is it?
questions.explanation: Apache Cassandra combines the BigTable column-family data model with a Dynamo-style peer-to-peer ring, giving an AP-oriented, masterless design.

questions.question: To triple throughput, the team adds three cheap commodity nodes to the cluster instead of upgrading one server's CPU and RAM. Which scaling property does this exploit?
questions.explanation: Horizontal scalability (scaling out) grows capacity by adding machines and redistributing data, the defining trait of most NoSQL systems, versus scaling up a single server.

questions.question: During a network partition, a cluster's minority side rejects all reads and writes rather than risk divergent data, keeping one authoritative copy on the majority side. Which CAP property did the system sacrifice?
questions.explanation: Refusing requests on the minority side preserves consistency (CP) at the cost of availability — those nodes cannot serve every request during the partition.

questions.question: For fire-and-forget metrics writes where latency matters more than durability, the coordinator reports success as soon as any single replica acknowledges. Which Cassandra consistency level is this?
questions.explanation: ONE requires only a single replica acknowledgment — the fastest, least durable option — versus QUORUM or ALL for stronger guarantees.

questions.question: A client connected to a sharded MongoDB cluster sends each query to a lightweight routing process, which consults config-server metadata and forwards it to the shard holding the data. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: The mongos router caches the cluster metadata from the config servers and directs each operation to the correct shard, making sharding transparent to clients.

questions.question: Every second, each Cassandra node exchanges state digests with a few random peers, so the whole cluster learns membership and failure information without any master node. Which protocol is this?
questions.explanation: The gossip protocol spreads node state epidemic-style through periodic peer exchanges, giving decentralized failure detection and topology discovery.

questions.question: Two replicas of a shopping cart were updated concurrently on different nodes; stored (node, counter) version stamps reveal that neither version subsumes the other, so a conflict must be resolved. Which mechanism detected this?
questions.explanation: Vector clocks track per-node version counters; two versions are concurrent when neither vector dominates the other, flagging a conflict for reconciliation.

questions.question: A Cassandra cluster has replication factor N = 3. For a workload using write consistency W and read consistency R to guarantee strong consistency, what inequality must hold?
alternatives: W plus R must exceed N
questions.explanation: When the write and read quorums overlap (W + R > N), every read set intersects the latest write set, so reads observe the most recent acknowledged write.

questions.question: In a sharded MongoDB cluster, chunks grow beyond the configured size and must be redistributed across shards. Which background process migrates chunks to keep shards balanced?
questions.explanation: MongoDB's balancer runs on the config server primary and migrates chunks between shards to equalize data distribution.

questions.question: A Redis-backed leaderboard must keep members ordered by score and support ZRANGE and ZREVRANK queries. Which Redis data structure is the right choice?
questions.explanation: Redis sorted sets pair each member with a score and keep them ordered, giving O(log N) rank and range operations ideal for leaderboards.

questions.question: A mobile app writes a profile update to replica A, then immediately reads from replica B and sees the old value. Which session consistency guarantee has been violated?
questions.explanation: Read-your-writes consistency guarantees a process always observes the effects of its own writes, even on other replicas.

questions.question: In a Dynamo-style system, node B is down when a write destined for it arrives, so node C stores the replica along with metadata naming the intended recipient and forwards it once B recovers. What is this mechanism called?
questions.explanation: Hinted handoff lets a healthy node temporarily hold a replica 'hinted' with the intended owner, preserving write availability during failures.
